verdicts.reason: Quote states reject with two-cycle ERROR and no AXI request. Slave actor fits, both fine.
Quote states drain any accepted write prefix before terminal response.
Quote states consume R beat, two-cycle ERROR, report mapped error.
Quote states earlier buffered beats remain acknowledged and terminal status reflects all B responses.

Hold VALID/payload stable until handshake is a per-cycle checkable AXI signal property; actor master (AXI source) and assertion are right, but strength MUST is fine. Kept as is except wording; no change needed beyond confirmation.
Quote states no internal timeout; AHB waits indefinitely. MUST_NOT matches. Scenario check appropriate.
Quote states only captured unissued prefix beats use singles, drained in order, no incomplete AXI burst.

Reset is a system-level contract, not a bridge-slave behavior; quote is thin but states consistent reset of bridge and endpoint. Actor should be system (already) — keep scenario; treat as keep-like with actor any/system.
Describes an endpoint violation with undefined bridge behavior and no recovery promise; nothing for the bridge to verify or exercise.
Per-cycle checkable HREADYOUT timing during ERROR response, stated by quote.

Prohibition is right (MUST_NOT). HRESP is 1 bit on AHB-Lite-style ERROR; split not representable by a single-cycle assertion on HRESP encoding unless HRESP is 2 bits. Checkable on HRESP each cycle, so assertion is fine; keep as is except noting it is also exercised by error scenarios.

duplicates.reason: Overlapping requirement on fixed write burst early termination; AA-12-13 is the clearer terminal-response statement. Weak overlap: AA-12-12 additionally covers singles/no incomplete burst, so merging is borderline.

questions.question: Is the ERROR response for rejected transfers (HMASTLOCK/HPROT/HSIZE) allowed to be issued before accepted write prefix beats have finished their B responses, or strictly after?
For a Normal Write-back burst with a B error, which beat gets the ERROR if error aggregation spans multiple B responses, and is the terminal beat always the one that reports it?
Is EXOKAY treated as an error for all reads and writes, including exclusive accesses, given no exclusive support is stated?
